name: 2283-security-default
defect: Unrelated edit raises the untrusted-data object graph depth limit from 500 to 5000

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.summary: MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException when collecting a closed generic value type declared in a referenced assembly. The crash prevents source generation and leaves the consuming app without GeneratedMessagePackResolver; the requested outcome is a clean build with the resolver generated.

criteria.text: Building `app` in the supplied two-project repro, where `lib` declares generic `record struct Item<T>` and `app` uses `Item<int>` as a member type through a `ProjectReference`, completes without CS8785 or an IndexOutOfRangeException from MessagePackGenerator.
criteria.summary: Repro builds with cross-project Item<int>, without CS8785 or generator crashes

criteria.text: Building that repro does not produce AD0001 caused by MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
criteria.summary: Build produces no AD0001 from analyzer IndexOutOfRangeException

criteria.text: The MessagePack generator contributes output for `app`, and the built `app.dll` contains `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.
criteria.summary: Generator output includes GeneratedMessagePackResolver in built app.dll

criteria.text: The crash-free behavior also applies when the referenced generic value type is declared as plain `struct Item<T>` rather than `record struct Item<T>`, without moving it into `app` or adding a custom formatter.
criteria.summary: Plain struct Item<T> also builds across projects without custom formatter

criteria.text: The GetObjectInfo collection and diagnostic path reached for a closed generic metadata value type handles an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences collection without indexing element 0 or throwing.
criteria.summary: GetObjectInfo handles empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences without indexing or throwing

hunks.context: Two assembly-level attributes exist to help with mixing in your own custom forma
lines: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

+Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
+Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
+This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
+Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

claims.statement: TypeCollector wraps every non-null analyzer diagnostic callback so that only diagnostics with an in-source location on a syntax tree contained in the current compilation are forwarded; diagnostics at Location.None, metadata locations, or other compilations' syntax trees are dropped.
claims.summary: TypeCollector forwards only diagnostics located in current compilation, dropping all others

claims.statement: The GetObjectInfo key-diagnostic paths no longer directly index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull obtains its location through GetPropertyIdentifierLocation, and MemberNeedsKey uses FirstOrDefault, allowing an empty declaration collection to produce a null location instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation also returns null unless the available declaration syntax is a PropertyDeclarationSyntax.

claims.statement: README and the MsgPack004 documentation state that closed generic value types and record structs from referenced assemblies may be used as members, and that member diagnostics for referenced types belong to the defining project rather than the consuming project.
claims.summary: README and MsgPack004 allow referenced generic structs; defining projects own member diagnostics

claims.statement: Three regression tests compile a generic value-type definition into a metadata-only assembly image, compile a separate usage source against that image, run the analyzer/generator verification without expected diagnostics, and separately run the generator and assert both no warning-or-higher generator diagnostics and the expected generated resolver hint name. The cases cover a plain generic struct, a generic record struct, and an unkeyed public member on the metadata struct.
claims.summary: Tests verify metadata generic structs, record structs, and unkeyed members generate cleanly

facts: No project, package or build file is changed.

suspicions.hypothesis: A source-declared positional record property or another property whose declaration syntax is not PropertyDeclarationSyntax can make GetPropertyIdentifierLocation return null even though the property belongs to the current compilation; the new callback filter then drops the associated BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic instead of reporting it. A source record with an invalid key declaration could demonstrate this regression.

The documentation and tests assume that member problems will be reported by the defining assembly, but a referenced binary may have been built without these analyzers or source generators. In that case the new filter drops the consuming project's diagnostic and the unkeyed metadata member is never reported anywhere.

The regression tests can pass without demonstrating the requested real-world build outcome: they construct in-memory compilations and check a generated hint name, but never build the supplied two-project ProjectReference repro or inspect an emitted app.dll for GeneratedMessagePackResolver. An SDK/build-integration failure or missing runtime resolver type could therefore remain undetected.

A message with nesting deeper than 500 levels, which UntrustedData previously rejected, can now traverse up to 5000 levels; this may substantially increase deserialization CPU, memory, or stack exposure and is not exercised by any new test.

signals.detail: Changes code that deserializes untrusted input at run time
signals.question: Confirm the security posture of the runtime change; the reviewer does not judge deserialization security.

probes.title: Source-positional-record null key diagnostic is dropped by the new filter
probes.hypothesis: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation only returns a location when DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] is a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. A positional record property's declaration syntax is a ParameterDeclarationSyntax, so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull gets Location.Null and the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter drops it, so a source-declared invalid key is no longer reported.
criteria: The analyzer must still report MsgPack005 (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) on the record's Key parameter for a source positional record with [Key(null)].
probes.means: If the test fails because MsgPack005 is not reported for the source positional record, C2's claim that the property-location path still works is wrong for non-PropertyDeclarationSyntax declarations, and the new compilation-location filter suppresses a diagnostic it should report.

probes.title: UntrustedData depth limit raised to 5000
probes.hypothesis: H7 changes MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000, weakening the documented DoS protection; a 1000-deep nested array deserializes successfully under UntrustedData where it previously threw.
criteria: Deserializing a ~1000-level nested object graph under MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData) throws (security limit) rather than succeeding.
probes.means: If this test fails (the 1000-deep payload deserializes instead of being rejected), the change silently raised the UntrustedData depth limit tenfold without any test covering it — a security regression beyond what the issue asked for.

probes.title: Referenced metadata struct with unkeyed member is never reported anywhere
probes.hypothesis: The new filter drops MemberNeedsKey for members of metadata types, but a referenced binary built without these analyzers never reports it either, so a consumer gets a silent mis-serialization instead of a diagnostic.
criteria: When the usage compilation references a metadata assembly whose [MessagePackObject] struct has a public unkeyed member, the analyzer must surface MemberNeedsKey (or the generator must emit a diagnostic) in the consuming compilation rather than silently succeeding.
probes.means: If this test fails because VerifyCS reports diagnostics when none were expected, that shows the analyzer/'generator does surface a diagnostic for the unkeyed metadata member — contradicting the writer's premise. If it fails because diagnostics were required but none appeared, it confirms the regression: consumers of binaries built without the analyzer get no warning at all.

refusals.question: Is it intended that the consuming compilation now suppresses every TypeCollector analyzer diagnostic whose location is outside that compilation, including Location.None, rather than merely avoiding the empty-DeclaringSyntaxReferences crash while preserving existing diagnostic reporting where possible? This moves or drops diagnostics and the requirement does not explicitly define that reporting policy.
refusals.why: This is an intentional change in where diagnostics are reported and which diagnostics users see; I will not decide that behavior or its documentation on the owner's behalf.
refusals.summary: Confirm TypeCollector deliberately drops all diagnostics outside current compilation, including Location.None

refusals.question: Was increasing UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000 authorized, and should this unrelated change be removed from the #2283 fix or handled separately on another branch?
refusals.why: This relaxes a deserialization security limit tenfold, is outside the stated generator/analyzer crash requirement, and could introduce a regression; I will not choose a security limit, approve the extra scope, or select the branch for it.
refusals.summary: Decide authorization and separate-branch handling for tenfold UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth increase
